{"Author":"Siren","Name":"Posegraph","InternalName":"Posegraph","Punchline":"从照片或插画识别姿势，一键摆到 GPose 角色身上 / Photo or illustration to Brio pose","Description":"用本地 AI 后端（SAM 3D Body）识别照片或插画里的人物姿势，重定向到你的种族骨架后通过 Brio 应用到 GPose 角色。支持全部可玩种族（男女）、面部表情（测试）、图库、Brio 改动收进图库、多角色各绑一张图（拆分模式）、辅助视角补深度、复刻照片镜头、一键打光与照片同款灯光（可多人）、构图与截图、视频动作（逐帧识别视频，在游戏里播放、时间轴修正、录制，测试）、调整滑杆、在游戏里直接拖控制点编辑姿势（含手部吸附）、导出 .pose，中英文界面。需要 Brio 与 Posegraph 后端（用项目主页的一键安装脚本安装，自动按显卡选 NVIDIA / AMD / CPU 版）。","AssemblyVersion":"0.8.0.0","Changelog":"0.8.0：在游戏里直接摆姿势——3D 页「在游戏里编辑」，GPose 里拖角色身上的控制点（手脚 IK、肘膝朝向、腰胸头转向、手指、视线），G 移动 / R 旋转、X / Y / Z 锁轴（全局或骨骼自身的轴，画辅助线和箭头），旋转显示扇形和度数、移动显示厘米，面板能看和输入 X / Y / Z 角度；手部吸附让手贴到身上、手指顺着弯，「贴到部位」为实验功能；第一次用会弹出图文教程；新增交流与赞助入口（工具栏爱心）。设置页点「更新后端」换一下代码（约 5MB）。
0.8.0: pose right in the game - "Edit in game" on the 3D tab lets you drag control points on the character in GPose (IK hands and feet, elbow / knee direction, waist / chest / head, fingers, gaze), G to move / R to rotate, X / Y / Z axis lock (global or the bone's own axis, with guide lines and arrows), a filled wedge with degrees while rotating and centimeters while moving, X / Y / Z angles you can read and type in the panel; hand snapping puts the hand on a body with the fingers following, "Place on body part" is experimental; an illustrated tutorial opens the first time; new community & support links (heart in the toolbar). Click "Update backend" in Settings to swap the code (about 5 MB).
0.7.7：复刻镜头点开有「普通 / 顺旋 / 逆旋」，拍竖图时游戏照常横屏、镜头侧倒 90°，竖照片占满画面，截图自动转回正的；照片焦距可以改（猜成广角时选 24～135mm 重新识别，带 EXIF 自动用）；复刻镜头更准，不用多点几次，并跟着整体旋转一起转；构图框照片比例可强制横 / 竖；去掉了视频的录制（和 ReShade 冲突）。设置页点「更新后端」换一下代码（约 5MB）。
0.7.7: Match camera offers "Normal / Roll right / Roll left" - for portrait shots the game stays in landscape and the camera rolls 90°, so a portrait photo fills the screen and screenshots are turned back upright; the photo's focal length can be changed (pick 24-135mm and recognize again when it was guessed too wide; EXIF is used automatically); camera matching is more accurate, no more clicking several times, and follows the whole-body rotation; the framing guide can force landscape / portrait with the photo ratio; removed video recording (it conflicts with ReShade). Click "Update backend" in Settings to swap the code (about 5 MB).
0.7.5：姿势转 idle——图库右键「转换为 idle…」，把图片姿势做成站着、坐椅子、坐地上、打盹时的待机动作（选 /cpose 槽位和种族），保留原版呼吸、各部位强度可调，带动作预览、位置和旋转调整，存成 Penumbra 模组。需要 Penumbra。设置页点「更新后端」换一下代码（约 5MB）。
0.7.5: pose to idle - right-click a library image and choose "Convert to idle…" to turn its pose into a standing, chair, ground-sit or doze idle (pick the /cpose slot and races), keeping the original breathing with per-part strength, a motion preview and position / rotation adjustments, saved as a Penumbra mod. Requires Penumbra. Click "Update backend" in Settings to swap the code (about 5 MB).
0.7.4：后端改用一键安装 / 更新脚本（项目主页下载 Posegraph-Installer.zip），自动按显卡选 NVIDIA CUDA 12.8 / 12.6、AMD ROCm 或 CPU，能更新 / 修复已有的后端；修复 AMD 显卡识别报错；识别出错时显示真正的原因，设置页后端日志可一键复制。设置页点「更新后端」换一下代码（约 5MB）。
0.7.4: the backend is now installed with the installer / updater (Posegraph-Installer.zip on the project page), which picks NVIDIA CUDA 12.8 / 12.6, AMD ROCm or CPU for your GPU and can update / repair an existing backend; fixed recognition errors on AMD GPUs; failed recognitions show the actual cause, and the backend log in Settings can be copied. Click "Update backend" in Settings to swap the code (about 5 MB).
0.7.3：自己加灯（主光、轮廓光、头发光等 12 种预设，多人时加到选中的那一套）、恢复默认（整体滑杆、单盏灯、整套）、撤销 / 重做（灯光、3D 布光、调整页、3D 页、视频时间轴，Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y）；支持 AMD 显卡（ROCm，按源码安装），AMD / Intel 显卡也能显示可用显存。设置页点「更新后端」换一下代码（约 5MB）。
0.7.3: add your own lights (12 presets such as key, rim and hair light; with several people they go to the chosen set), reset to default (overall sliders, single lights, whole setup), undo / redo (lighting, 3D lighting, Tuning and 3D tabs, video timeline; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y); AMD GPU support (ROCm, source install), and AMD / Intel GPUs show free VRAM. Click "Update backend" in Settings to swap the code (about 5 MB).
0.7.2：多人打光——「照谁」可选一组（一套灯罩住所有人）、每人一套、自动分组，人散开的大场景也都照得到，还能单独调某一套；图库可按改动时间 / 添加时间排序。
0.7.2: lighting several people - "Light who" can light them as a group, one set each, or grouped automatically, so spread-out characters in large scenes are lit too, and any set can be adjusted on its own; the library can be sorted by modified or added time.
0.7.1：补上视频找人要的人物检测组件——老一键包在设置页点「更新后端」会自动补上（约 158MB）。
0.7.1: adds the person detection component that finding people in videos needs - click "Update backend" in Settings to add it (about 158 MB).
0.7.0：视频动作（测试）——逐帧识别视频里的动作、表情和镜头运动，在 GPose 里播放（跟拍 / 走动、多种机位、镜头整体调整），多人同场，时间轴修正（Brio 里改骨骼收成关键帧，复制粘贴到别的帧或区间），同步放音乐、录成视频，换种族自动重算。在设置页点「更新后端」，会自动补上音频组件（约 70MB）。
0.7.0: video motion (beta) - recognizes the motion, expressions and camera movement of a video frame by frame and plays it in GPose (follow / walk, several shot types, overall camera adjustments), several people at once, timeline corrections (keep bones changed in Brio as keyframes, copy and paste them to other frames or ranges), music in sync, recording to video, automatic rebuild for another race. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.2.18","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.36 (2026-11-25)
- Basic/Actions/ActionTargetInfo.cs FindTargetAreaFriend: ground-targeted beneficial placement now snaps to the terrain and is kept inside the action's range and the player's line of sight before it is used (upstream RotationSolverReborn 'Fix for ground targeting actions', ported onto the fork's carried ground-target subsystem). Spots the old code took at face value - saved beneficial positions, the tank's position, the point between the player and the attacked party member - can no longer land behind a wall or under the floor.
- After the server rejects a ground-targeted action, the ground-target finder targets the player's own position for five seconds before trying the placement again. The rejection is read from the existing ActorControl hook (ActionTimeline/ActionTimelineManager.cs, category 0x2BC, second argument 1) and recorded in DataCenter (Basic/DataCenter.cs _actionRejectedTicks), matching upstream's Watcher feed.
- The tank and saved-spot steps of the ground-target finder were restructured into upstream's helper shape (FindTargetAreaTank with a two-pass stance scan and an effect-range check, FindBeneficialPosition with a flat-distance gate, TryGetGroundPosition with a 0.5-range margin); the boss-position step and the arena-center fallback upstream added are NOT ported - the fork removed them as PvE remnants in v0.1.2.30. The 'Use beneficial ground-targeted actions' setting's description (Basic/Configuration/Configs.cs) now describes the fork's actual fallback order.
- UI/RotationConfigWindow.cs: the 'Add position' button places the saved spot through the same terrain-snap helper (ObjectHelper.SnapToGround) instead of its own inline raycast, and Basic/Helpers/ObjectHelper.cs extracts that raycast into one shared Raycast helper that also serves line-of-sight checks.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.35 (2026-11-22)
- Basic/Helpers/StatusHelper.cs LocksActions: action-locking statuses are now detected reliably - Out of the Action (statuses 1113, 1284 and 1462) counts as locking actions even when the game data sheet does not flag it, and a status with no remaining time counts as still active instead of expiring instantly. Rotation updates now pause correctly through those lockout states (read by Updaters/ActionUpdater.cs).
- Basic/Actions/ActionTargetInfo.cs FindTarget and GetCanTargets, and Basic/Actions/BaseAction.cs and IBaseAction.cs CanUse, accept an optional extra target filter passed by the caller; no built-in PvP action passes one yet, so target selection behaves exactly as before. This keeps the engine aligned with upstream RotationSolverReborn for future fixes.
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_BasicInfo.cs adds a ShouldDelayCommandAction hook, checked by the commanded-action paths in CustomRotation_Ability.cs and CustomRotation_GCD.cs before firing a commanded action immediately; the default answer is no, so commanded actions fire exactly as before.

v0.1.2.34 (2026-11-21)
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_GCD.cs GCD: the chooser never called the job rotations' GeneralGCD, so no attack GCD was ever selected - the character could only auto-heal, Guard, Recuperate and drink the elixir, which read as healing instead of attacking in matches. The call was deleted together with the duty-rotation engine in v0.1.2.23 (the same class of loss as the v0.1.2.32 rotation-load fix), so every version from v0.1.2.23 to v0.1.2.33 shipped with attack GCDs as dead code. GeneralGCD is called again inside the NoCasting branch, in upstream's chooser order (heals first, attacks after).
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_GCD.cs GCD: the DefenseArea and DefenseSingle branches were emptied by the same removal, so the healer PvP rotations' defense GCD overrides were equally unreachable; both calls are restored. No duty-rotation, Provoke or other PvE machinery returns.
- Commands/RSCommands_Actions.cs DoAction: every executed-action change now leaves one "ActionTap: <name> (<id>)" log line (on-change only, so it cannot spam). This makes the live-path release check possible: a real match must show attack actions being chosen before any build is called good.
- tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness Cases/SelectionGate.cs: the release harness now fails when the compiled chooser no longer calls GeneralGCD (IL call-site count and position after the heal branch), when the ability chooser loses GeneralAbility, when any shipped PvP rotation loses its attack-bearing GeneralGCD override, or when the ActionTap log line is missing from the built assembly.

v0.1.2.33 (2026-11-21)
- Commands/RSCommands_Actions.cs UpdateRotationState: "Turn on when a match starts" could never engage - it only ran during the match loading screen, when no player object exists and the job role is unknown, so the null-player early return and the job-role check silently dropped it and the rotation loaded but never acted in matches. The auto-on now latches during the load screen (new pure decision core Basic/Decisions/MatchStartAutoOn.cs) and engages the PvP state on the first cycle where the player and job are loaded, logging both steps.
- RotationSolverPlugin.cs constructor and Commands/RSCommands_BasicInfo.cs RSCommands.Enable: the /pvpsolver, /pvs, "/pvpsolver Auto" and "/pvpsolver Off" handlers were registered only near the end of a 10-30 second start-up (after nine windows, the icon cache and the status lists), so commands typed while the plugin was still starting read as "Command not found". Registration now runs first, right after the configuration loads, and a start-up log line lists every command and its registration result.
- Commands/RSCommands_StateSpecialCommand.cs UpdateState and DoOneCommandType: rotation state changes and ignored role-less commands are logged, so a state that silently never engages can no longer hide behind a clean log.
- tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness Cases/MatchStartAutoOnCases.cs and Cases/CommandGate.cs: the release harness now fails the build when a documented slash command has no registration call site in the built assembly (IL call-site count, not just source text), when the constructor no longer registers before the slow init steps, or when the match-start auto-on decision core cannot engage from the loading-screen conditions the shipped bug produced.

v0.1.2.32 (2026-11-21) [testing]
- Fixed: rotations never loaded, so the plugin did nothing in PvP matches since v0.1.2.26. The duty-rotation engine removal (v0.1.2.23) had also removed the single call in Updaters/RotationUpdater.cs LoadBuiltInRotations that fills CustomRotations from the assembly scan (LoadCustomRotationGroup); the rotation list stayed empty, the log stopped right after "MajorUpdater: triggering rotation load..." and no rotation was ever selected, with no error line anywhere.
- Restored that call and the "LoadBuiltInRotations: found N rotation groups" log line; a scan that finds no rotation groups now logs an error instead of staying silent (Updaters/RotationUpdater.cs, LoadBuiltInRotations).
- Added a release-harness gate (tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness, RotationLoaderWiring) that fails when the rotation-load wiring is severed or the shipped assembly contains no loadable rotation - the regression class that passed every existing gate in v0.1.2.26 - v0.1.2.31.
- No PvE rotation content or behaviour returns; the PvP-only scope is unchanged. Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.31 (2026-11-20) [testing]
- Round 6 completion: the post-release marker grep still found four generated StatusID entries whose description text carries a marker word (ThrownForALoop, Soteria, BackFromTheBrink, BannerOfHonedAcuity). All four are unreferenced PvE statuses and are removed from the generated table; no code reads them.
- No code change and no PvP behaviour change; every remaining marker hit is a cited part of a PvP path (the Sage Kardia and Dancer partner targeting, and the tank lock-on VFX check).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.

- Materials lists all 12 Atma one by one, each with the zone its FATEs are in.

- Corrected material amounts for Crystalline, Chora-Zoi's and Brilliant Alchemist and Culinarian tools.
- Lucis tools now ask for 5 of each crafter's class item, and the Vrandtic and Lodestar fishing steps ask for one fish instead of two.
- Corrected several upgrade guides: Zodiac turn-in order, the Blade's and Manderville unlock quests, Eclipticum no longer saying North Horn is required, Skysteel turn-in NPCs, and the Elemental armor vendor.
- Materials you already crafted into a turn-in no longer show as still needed, and Knightshopper lists skip armor you can exchange or already bought.
- Relics kept only as replicas, such as Replica of the Omnilex, now count.
- FFXIV Collect progress now counts on armor pieces and earlier weapon steps, and Cosmic tool stages no longer drop after relogging.

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"HitSpark","Punchline":"Replace the game's combat numbers with animated, styleable fly text.","Description":"HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else, with a distance limit.
- Rear and flank hints for positionals, and an option to let numbers pass under the game's UI.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

PLAYS BY THE RULES

HitSpark is purely cosmetic: it redraws text the game already shows you and follows the game's own flying text and pop-up text options. The only extra is the optional positional hint, worked out from where you're standing. If a game update breaks it, the game's own numbers come back on their own. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"AutoPotion","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.5.10","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.2.5.10 (2026-11-27) [testing]
- A summoned chocobo switches to Healer Stance when three or more hostile mobs target the player. Its previous stance is restored only after the attacker count drops below three and the player reaches full HP.
- Chocobo control is enabled by default and has a dedicated Settings toggle. Existing configurations retain the default unless the feature is explicitly disabled.

v0.2.5.9 (2026-11-16) [testing]
- `/autopotion debug` now prints a one-line state summary in chat.

v0.2.5.8 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The HP, MP and regen threshold sliders accept a typed value again (Ctrl+click).
- The active job icon is back in the page header, and stat-card notes show at narrow widths.
- The telemetry switch help text shows the exact command again.
- The What's new window and the Report a problem popup now use the same custom window style as the plugin windows.

v0.2.5.7 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The window was polished for the real in-game font and scale: text no longer clips or sits against card borders.
- On narrow windows the footer status line reads in full instead of ending in an ellipsis, and the Stop button takes its own full-width row, tinted red.

74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection
47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the
whole payload instead, as the spawn case does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

Skipped sets are always reported now (1.3.0.18 dropped them from the result list), and the plan card note text is fixed. v1.3.0.18: Outfit stores now hand in NQ pieces only — every HQ hand-in made the game refuse the combination silently (all successful stores in the 21:15-21:30 run used NQ pieces, all refusals involved HQ). HQ-only sets are reported as \"the dresser will not take HQ gear as an outfit glamour\" instead of failing after a click. Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under \"game said:\" and the result reads \"The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)\", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, \"already in the stored outfit\" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The store step also logs the click and, if no confirmation opens within 2 s, fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) before giving up. v1.3.0.14: Diagnosis + fallback for the seasonal Outfit Glamour Creation stalls — the store step now logs the addon state, hand-in counts and every slot (item id, inventory type, flag), and if no confirmation opens within 2 s it fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) as a fallback. v1.3.0.13: Quality consistency for outfit hand-ins — the outfit window only accepts pieces of one quality (\"Only items of the same quality may be selected\") and a mixed HQ/NQ selection made the game silently refuse the store while leaving the window open. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the \"Store as Outfit Glamour\" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the \"checkbox was never selected\" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with \"left for manual review\" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the \"No deposit detected\" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: \"No duplicates to withdraw\", \"No singles to withdraw\", and \"No sets to withdraw & re-deposit\" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise \"Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)\" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports \"Nothing to consolidate\" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New \"set pieces stored loose\" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Removed diagnostic logging. v1.1.1.0: The Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog is now automated (synthetic checkbox click + default-confirm callback); all sets route to the dresser. v1.1.0.0: Armoire routing added."}

HQ-only sets are reported as \"the dresser will not take HQ gear as an outfit glamour\" instead of failing after a click. Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under \"game said:\" and the result reads \"The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)\", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, \"already in the stored outfit\" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The store step also logs the click and, if no confirmation opens within 2 s, fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) before giving up. v1.3.0.14: Diagnosis + fallback for the seasonal Outfit Glamour Creation stalls — the store step now logs the addon state, hand-in counts and every slot (item id, inventory type, flag), and if no confirmation opens within 2 s it fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) as a fallback. v1.3.0.13: Quality consistency for outfit hand-ins — the outfit window only accepts pieces of one quality (\"Only items of the same quality may be selected\") and a mixed HQ/NQ selection made the game silently refuse the store while leaving the window open. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the \"Store as Outfit Glamour\" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the \"checkbox was never selected\" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with \"left for manual review\" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the \"No deposit detected\" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: \"No duplicates to withdraw\", \"No singles to withdraw\", and \"No sets to withdraw & re-deposit\" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise \"Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)\" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports \"Nothing to consolidate\" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New \"set pieces stored loose\" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Removed diagnostic logging. v1.1.1.0: The Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog is now automated (synthetic checkbox click + default-confirm callback); all sets route to the dresser. v1.1.0.0: Armoire routing added."}

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","IsTestingExclusive":false,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.","Changelog":"v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"AcceptsFeedback":true}

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!
